text.p: The Malta stock exchange share index rose 2.52 points in the once-a-week trading session on Wednesday, with Lombard bank (Malta) accounting for most of the gains and Mid-Med bank most of the volume.

Trading resulting in a total turnover of Lm209,707 ($576,694) from Lm202,200 ($556,050) over the pervious week. Business was speard over 75 deals, of which 49 were in equities and 26 in fixed income securities.

Business in equities amounted to just under Lm155,300, with 116,249 shares changing hands. Of these, 37,904 were Bank of Valletta shares transacted in 25 deals foir an average of 129.1 cents per share, unchanged.

There were 13 deals in Med-Med Bank with 63,714 sares being traded for an average 151.8 cents per share, down two mils. Two deals in Lombard Bank Malta saw 846 shares sold for an average 146.4 cents per share, up from 144.4 cents last week.
In Middle Sea Insurance, six deals were struck, with 1,825 shares sold for an average 122.7 cents per share, up seven mils since last traded on October 2.
Farsons ordinary shares lost a cent, with 11,960 shares selling for an average 52 cents per share.
In the government bond market, nine issues were dealt in, turnover reaching Lm53,600. Business was mainly in the 7.25 percent MGS2006(II).
In corporate bonds, there was one deal in the 6.5 percent Gasan Bonds 1998/99 moiunting to Lm 788.
